note: SNG (world-design 2026-07-22, Erik direction): morally-clean adversaries — things a character can fight and kill without it being a person with a story. Three classes. Power-tiered (riffraff/notable/regional/epic) to scale. Each entry carries the tradition-function families it PRESSURES (so the fight tests craft, not just HP) and the arc it reads from. This is the GM's pool for 'something to fight' that doesn't cost the player a moral choice — the counterpart to the challenger_pool (which is people) and legends (which are named figures).
designLaws: No person. A bestiary entry has no name of its own, no want, no story being ended. If it would be a tragedy to kill, it belongs in NPCs, not here.
A hazard, not a villain. Its 'motivation' is at most an instinct or a broken directive — never a grievance, never a plea.

Every entry pressures FUNCTION FAMILIES, not just deals damage. A fight should ask something of the character's craft — a thing that must be sensed, unmade, warded, or outmaneuvered, so 22 of 24 traditions that don't fight-by-hitting still have a way in.
Tied to the world. Each class reads from an arc — killing them is also reading the world's temperature.

manifested_creature.concept: A creature bled out of native fiction by the Manifestation Storm — a thing from a domain that manifested wrong, 'wrong for here,' flagged by how badly it fits the place it's in. Not evil; misplaced, and dangerous the way a wild animal in a kitchen is dangerous.
manifested_creature.morallyClean: It was dreamed into being by the substrate, not born. Ending it returns borrowed fiction; there is no one to mourn.

kit.name: the wrong-shaped blow
kit.why: it does not fit here and neither does the way it hits you

kit.name: almost not there
kit.why: ⚑ 'flagged by how badly it fits the place it's in' — and it half-doesn't

kit.name: the domain leaking
kit.why: ⚠️ it brings its own grammar with it

manifested_creature._kitWhy: ⛔ NOT EVIL, MISPLACED. Its danger is that the rules it obeys are somewhere else's.

feral_construct.concept: A mechanism whose maker is gone and whose directive rots — a pre-Transition device or Enginewright construct still running an order it no longer understands, turned dangerous by a purpose with no one to serve.
feral_construct.morallyClean: It is a broken tool, not a mind. Stopping it is repair by other means; the only tragedy is the maker who left it, and they are long gone.

kit.name: the order, still running
kit.why: ⚑ 'a purpose with no one to serve' — it is executing

kit.name: built to last
kit.why: a pre-Transition device outlives what it was for

kit.name: the procedure applied to you
kit.why: ⛔ it is not fighting you, it is PROCESSING you

feral_construct._kitWhy: ⚠️ `deathSave.notForClasses` bars it — there is no thread to cut. ⛑ And the kit says why: nothing here is alive to stop.

substrate_warped_beast.concept: A real animal the stirring substrate touched — a wolf, a river-thing, a bird-flock — warped past its own nature into something that hunts wrong and cannot be calmed. The saddest of the three, but past saving: the animal it was is already gone.
substrate_warped_beast.morallyClean: The creature it was is already lost to the warp. A clean end is the last mercy its original nature can be given — closer to putting down than to killing.

kit.name: hunting wrong
kit.why: ⚑ 'warped past its own nature into something that hunts wrong'

kit.name: faster than the animal was
kit.why: the substrate gave it something

kit.name: cannot be calmed
kit.why: ⛔ 'past saving' — soothe finds nothing to settle

substrate_warped_beast._kitWhy: ⚠️ THE SADDEST OF THE THREE and the kit should feel like an animal, not a monster: it strikes, it moves, and it will not stop.

made_weapon.concept: A person who has unmade themselves into a weapon — an assassin bound to a contract they can no longer refuse, a cultist hollowed by the cult-of-purity of their own tradition, a warden turned by the thing they warded. Clean to kill NOT because they were never a person, but because the person is already gone: what's left is the function. The design law holds by a hair — there is no story left to end, only a hand that will not stop.
made_weapon.designNote: The one class where the adversary wears a face. It stays clean ONLY when the person is genuinely foreclosed — a made instrument, not a soul mid-choice. If it would be a tragedy, it's an NPC, not this. Use sparingly; the horror is that a person CAN become this.

kit.name: the contract, kept
kit.why: ⛔ 'bound to a contract they can no longer refuse'

kit.name: what a person was
kit.why: ⚑ IT WAS SOMEONE — it still reads a fight like a person does

kit.name: nothing left to appeal to
kit.why: ⚠️ hollowed by the cult-of-purity of their own tradition

made_weapon._kitWhy: ⛑ THE ONLY BEAST THAT KEEPS A PERSON'S SKILL. `deathSave.notForClasses` bars it too — there is a body and no self.

great_manifestation.concept: The largest things the Storm bled through or the substrate raised — dragon-scale manifestations of a whole domain's logic given hunger and wing. Not an animal grown big: a piece of the world's grammar walking, the size of a hill, that resolved wrong and will not resolve back. A dragon is a domain that learned to fly and forgot everything but appetite.
great_manifestation._notAllDragons_20260908: ⛔ ERIK 2026-09-08: 'DRAGONS ARE NOT ALL POLES THAT WENT WRONG.' ⚑ A `great_manifestation` is ONE KIND — a domain that resolved wrong and will not resolve back, a hazard with a broken directive and no grievance. ⚠️ THE OTHER KIND IS A PERSON: a TRUE DRAGON, older than the Transition, wearing whichever shape the conversation needs. ⛑ AND THIS FILE'S OWN FIRST LAW IS THE TEST, UNCHANGED: 'no name of its own, no want, no story being ended — IF IT WOULD BE A TRAGEDY TO KILL, IT BELONGS IN NPCs, NOT HERE.' ⚑ Ysenkar and Tolvess have names, wants and stories that can end badly, so they are `npcs/`, and the line held without moving. ⬜ A manifestation-dragon and a true dragon can share a sky and are not the same kind of thing.

kit.name: the grammar landing
kit.why: ⚑ 'a piece of the world's grammar walking, the size of a hill'

kit.name: the domain asserting itself
kit.why: ⛔ it does not enter a place, it OVERWRITES one

kit.name: what a whole domain is
kit.why: ⚠️ you are hitting a rule, not an animal

great_manifestation._kitWhy: ⛔ A DOMAIN THAT RESOLVED WRONG AND WILL NOT RESOLVE BACK. ⚑ The `ward` is not armour — it is that the thing IS its own law.

narrowed_dead.concept: ⛔ A RAISING THAT WENT THE OTHER WAY. SPEC §48 gives two end states: STABLE (Afterlings, full personality) and NARROWING (unminded purpose). ⚠️ AN AFTERLING BELONGS IN NPCs — it is a person and killing it is a tragedy, which the design laws exclude from here. THE NARROWED DO NOT: what is left is an errand wearing a body, and that is a hazard.
narrowed_dead.morallyClean: ✅ CLEAN. There is no person left to wrong — which is the whole difference between this class and an Afterling, and the reason one is a creature and the other is an NPC.
narrowed_dead._shapeFix_20260830: ⚠️ I AUTHORED THIS CLASS AS A BARE STRING while the other five are objects with `concept` / `readsFromArc` / `morallyClean`. ⛔ ANYTHING READING `classes[x].concept` GOT `undefined` FOR THE NEWEST CLASS — and it is the one class whose concept a rule would most want to read. CCode found it: 'exactly the shape that makes a property unreadable later, so fix it BEFORE anything reads classes rather than after.' ✅ The original string is preserved verbatim as `concept`.

kit.name: the one purpose left
kit.why: ⚑ 'unminded purpose' — everything else narrowed away

kit.name: it knows what it was for
kit.why: ⛔ narrowing keeps the errand and drops the person

kit.name: already past the worst
kit.why: ⚠️ it has been dying for a while

narrowed_dead._kitWhy: ⛑ AND `deathSave` DELIBERATELY DOES NOT BAR IT (R29): there is still a thread there, and that is the whole horror of the class.

classes._hasSelf_20260830: ⛔ `hasSelf` — ONE PROPERTY, NOT A TAXONOMY. CCode measured 2026-08-30 that a creature-type system predicting resistances would COMPLICATE: affinities do not cluster by class ('the_ashen_wyrm RESISTS light, the_bright_devourer ABSORBS it — SAME CLASS, opposite relationships'), so a class default would be wrong more often than right and every exception would need an override. ✅ THIS IS THE OTHER CHANGE: seven crafts already say 'nothing without a self can be frightened' IN FOUR DIFFERENT PHRASINGS, and `the_narrowed` says the other half as `feeling: immune` in data. NOTHING CHECKS THE TWO AGREE AND NOTHING EVER WILL WHILE ONE SIDE IS PROSE. ⚠️ THE TEST ERIK SET, AND IT IS THE RIGHT ONE: does it let content say ONCE what it currently says many times in prose? ⛔ If it only lets us predict a number, it is a layer. ✅ `hasSelf: false` — narrowed_dead, feral_construct, made_weapon. A thing driven by an errand or a mechanism has nobody home to frighten. ✅ `hasSelf: true` — manifested_creature, substrate_warped_beast, great_manifestation: manifested things WANT, and a warped beast is still a beast.
classes._psychicResist_20260830: ⛔ EVERY `hasSelf: false` CREATURE CARRIES `psychic: resist`. Erik 2026-08-30, on psychic_lance: 'it seems like that one MIGHT STILL HAVE SOME IMPACT even if the thing doesn't have a mind.' ⚠️ SOME IMPACT, NOT NONE AND NOT FULL — and `resist` is the only verdict that says that. A craft-level `requiresSelf` is BINARY and could not express it. ✅ THE THOUGHT IS REAL AND ARRIVES; THERE IS SIMPLY LESS FOR IT TO FIND. ⚠️ AUTHORED PER-CREATURE RATHER THAN DERIVED FROM THE CLASS, because a class-level affinity DEFAULT is the thing CCode measured against on 08-30: affinities do not cluster, and a default would need overrides. ⛔ THIS IS A DELIBERATE EXCEPTION AND WORTH REVISITING IF A SELFLESS CREATURE SHOULD EVER BE FULLY OPEN TO PSYCHIC HARM — the per-creature field is what makes that possible.

storied_beast.concept: A creature out of a story. When the Storm came through, what the peoples had told each other in the dark for generations came true: the grave-eaters the Ashwardens warned their children about, the Rootkin's briar-bear, the Blazeborn's pyre-hounds, the Masons' gargoyles. Each tradition's folklore became fauna in its own lands, and then it spread along the roads.
storied_beast.morallyClean: It is the story, not a someone: a shape the Storm poured a people's belief into. It has an animal's hunger or a tale's rule, never a grievance. If it could be reasoned with as a person, it would belong in NPCs.

kit.name: the tale's teeth
kit.why: every story creature has the one thing it does to you

kit.name: what the story says it is
kit.why: it is exactly as hard to hurt as the tale says

kit.name: the story's rule
kit.why: ⚑ and it is bound by its tale: the rule the people told about it (storyRule) is TRUE, and knowing it is the edge

storied_beast._whyThisClass: SNG-661 (Erik 2026-09-26: 'think of all the types of creatures in the monster compendiums of games like this... those would likely exist here in all kinds of different areas because the people manifested them'). The in-world reason is the Manifestation Storm: belief made real. That is why each creature carries `storiedBy` (whose story), `habitat` (where it lives, matched against place tags) and `storyRule` (the folk-remedy from the tale, which works).

lattice_keeper.concept: What the Lattice sends to keep its own. The 26 waygates were laid in one act by something that did not need to try twice, and they have never been anyone's. When someone takes one (puts men on the arch, charges for passage, closes it) the gate itself answers: first it misbehaves, then things come through it for whoever is holding it, a little worse each season, until they let go.
lattice_keeper.morallyClean: There is no one in there. A keeper is the network's maintenance, wearing a shape, and it has no grievance and no mercy. It cannot be bargained with or turned, only outlasted or answered by releasing the gate. It never pursues past the gate's yard, and it never comes for a gate nobody holds.
lattice_keeper._why: SNG-663 Â§2c (Erik 2026-09-26: 'Both stigma AND consequence of something coming for you from the gate... the gate keeps of some sort').

roster.name: glimmerlings
roster.look: A flickering swarm of palm-sized things that are almost birds, almost lights, almost nothing — bled from a domain of pure attention.
roster.danger: Individually harmless; a swarm blinds and disorients, and they feed on whatever a person is looking at.
roster.clean: They wink out like the fiction they are. No blood, no cry.

roster.name: a hollow-pace
roster.look: A waist-high walking frame, pre-Transition, still executing a patrol route for a wall that fell centuries ago. Rusted, patient, wrong.
roster.danger: Strikes anything that crosses its dead route; relentless, tireless, no judgment left in it.
roster.clean: You are switching off a machine that forgot how to stop. Its maker mourned it long ago.

roster.name: a warpling
roster.look: Was a hare. Is now too many legs and a hunger that doesn't match its size, moving in stutters the eye can't track.
roster.danger: Fast, erratic, bites what it can't eat; travels in warped warrens.
roster.clean: The hare is already gone. What's left is a wound wearing its shape.

roster.name: the wrong stag
roster.look: A great beast that was a stag, antlers grown into a lattice that hums, eyes that track things not present. It walks the tree-line and the wood goes quiet.
roster.danger: Charges with the lattice leading; the hum unmakes small craft; it does not flee and cannot be driven.
roster.clean: The old stag of the wood would weep to see it. Ending it is the mercy the warp denied.

roster.name: a tessellith
roster.look: A block-logic manifestation the size of a cart — matter that resolved into a crawling geometry of interlocking units, bled from the Blocklands seam.
roster.danger: Resolves what it touches into its own grammar — ground, tools, a careless limb — growing as it goes.
roster.clean: It is the bleed made flesh — geometry, not a being. You are correcting a grammar error that grew teeth.

roster.name: the unmoored choir
roster.look: A domain-scale manifestation: a drifting region of half-formed voices and light where a bloom set WRONG, a place that is almost a creature and almost a weather.
roster.danger: Everything inside it starts to un-belong — craft frays, memory loosens, the self blurs toward the choir. It spreads at its edges.
roster.clean: A birth that went wrong and never became anyone. Ending it is the stemming 'Present at the Birth' offers — grief for a wonder, not a death.

roster.name: a cinder-mote drift
roster.look: A low cloud of orange sparks that drifts like it's thinking, settling on anything that will catch. Blazeborn radiance bled loose and gone stupid.
roster.danger: Ignites what it touches; swarms toward the brightest heat, including yours.
roster.clean: Light with no eye behind it. Snuffing it is housekeeping.

roster.name: rust-choir gnats
roster.look: A cloud of thumbnail-sized repair-drones, makers long gone, still trying to 'fix' — welding shut what should be open, patching flesh like it's hull.
roster.danger: Swarms a wound or a seam and 'mends' it wrong; individually nothing, together a slow ruin.
roster.clean: A directive with no maker. Ending it frees nothing that can feel freed.

roster.name: a mire-gulper
roster.look: Was a bottom-feeding fish; is now a mouth on four crawling fins, hauling itself up the bank after warmth.
roster.danger: Ambushes from mud; a bite that doesn't let go; comes in numbers where the water's gone wrong.
roster.clean: A hunger that outgrew its body. No mercy owed, none possible.

roster.name: a pale reader
roster.look: A thin, translucent figure-shape that copies whatever craft it last saw, badly — a manifested echo of Cogitant memory, running a stolen gesture on loop.
roster.danger: Mimics your last ability at half strength and turns it back on you; unsettling, not deadly, until three of them agree.
roster.clean: An echo of a thought no one is thinking. Silencing it ends nothing.

roster.name: a gloamwolf pack
roster.look: Wolves the dark got into — coats that drink light, eyes gone flat black, moving in a silence that's wrong for that many bodies.
roster.danger: Coordinated, patient, drives prey toward the ones waiting; the pack thinks as one and the one is hungry.
roster.clean: Wolves are honest. These aren't wolves anymore. End it and the wood can have its wolves back.

roster.name: a toll-wraith
roster.look: A road-shaped grievance manifested — Marcher discipline bled into a thing that guards a crossing that no longer exists, and charges the living to pass.
roster.danger: Blocks a path and demands a price in blood or memory; will not be reasoned with, only paid or beaten.
roster.clean: A rule with no ruler, guarding a gate that fell. Breaking it opens the road.

roster.name: a lantern-ambusher
roster.look: A pre-Transition sentry-frame, one lamp-eye still lit, that learned the light draws the lost — and waits where it drew them.
roster.danger: Lures with a warm light in bad country, then falls on what comes; patient, positioned, cold.
roster.clean: A trap that outlived its war. It baits; it doesn't grieve.

roster.name: a weeping stone
roster.look: A Threnodist grief manifested into slow-moving rock that leaks sorrow like water — everything near it slows, saddens, forgets why it was hurrying.
roster.danger: Not a striker — a drainer; the longer you're near, the less you can act, until you sit down beside it and stop.
roster.clean: Feeling with no one feeling it. Ending it is a mercy to everyone in earshot.

roster.name: a quill-swarm
roster.look: A flock of small birds warped into flying blades — feathers gone to hardened spines, moving as one turning sheet.
roster.danger: Attacks in a wave, banks, comes again; open ground is death, cover is survival.
roster.clean: A murmuration with the murmur gone to malice. Scattering it is clean.

roster.name: the kept hunger
roster.look: An Ashwarden-made containment vessel whose seal rotted — the last thing it was keeping is loose inside it, and it walks now looking for more to keep.
roster.danger: Tries to 'contain' the living — a grip that stills, a cold that keeps; what it holds, it does not release.
roster.clean: A jar that learned to hunt. What's inside was ended long ago; this only echoes it.

roster.name: a glass-stalker
roster.look: A Verist-truth manifestation — a near-invisible predator of clear planes that you see only in reflection or by the wrongness it bends around itself.
roster.danger: Strikes from the angle you're not looking; the only defense is knowing it's there before it moves.
pressures: HARM (hit what you can barely see)
roster.clean: A truth so plain it's invisible, gone predatory. Seeing it kill it is the whole fight.

roster.name: a churn-revel
roster.look: Churnfolk chaos manifested into a rolling knot of improvised limbs and salvage, laughing in a language of breaking things, never the same shape twice.
roster.danger: Unpredictable by nature — no read holds two beats; it's the fight where planning fails and reflex wins.
roster.clean: Joy with nothing behind the laugh. Ending it quiets a wrongness, not a soul.

roster.name: the Unrefusing Blade
roster.look: An assassin bound to a Lattice-contract they can no longer break — the person spent, the contract still running them. Moves with a terrible economy; every motion is the shortest line to your death.
roster.danger: No wasted act, no tell, no mercy and no cruelty — just the function. Reads YOUR craft and pre-empts it.
pressures: HARM (end it before it ends you)
SWAY (there is nothing left to sway — and learning that IS the fight)
roster.clean: The person who took the contract is gone; the contract wears their hands. You are not killing them. You are ending what took their place.

roster.name: the Pure-of-Ash
roster.look: An Ashwarden hollowed by their own cult-of-purity — one who decided the mercy of stopping should be given to EVERYONE, unasked. Grey-robed, calm, and utterly certain.
roster.danger: Wields real Palework turned to murder; believes each kill is a kindness; cannot be argued out of a certainty that is all that's left of them.
pressures: SWAY (test whether any person remains — the answer is no)
roster.clean: The cult-of-purity ate the warden. What's left administers death as doctrine. Ending it is the mercy they forgot how to withhold.

roster.name: the Severed Choir
roster.look: A Seraphic order-member who cut away their own doubt to become pure instrument of judgment — armored in certainty, voice a chord that compels, eyes that have decided about you already.
roster.danger: Compels with choral force (obey, kneel, stop); judges in absolutes; the fight is as much against agreeing with it as against its blade.
roster.clean: They severed the part that could be wrong. What judges you now is a verdict, not a person. There is no one left to appeal to — only the sentence to end.

roster.name: the Gearfather
roster.look: A pre-Transition foundational engine woken feral — building-sized, still trying to 'complete' a project whose plans rotted, assembling anything nearby into its endless wrong construction.
roster.danger: Reaches with crane-arms to add you to the build; the ground is its body; you fight it by fighting the place.
roster.clean: A maker with no plan and no maker. It builds nothing and won't stop. Ending it lets the ground be ground.

roster.name: the Bloom-That-Hungers
roster.look: A Rootkin growth gone predatory — a hill-sized flowering mass that lures with impossible beauty and fruit, and feeds on what comes to eat.
roster.danger: Beauty as bait, tendrils as jaws, spores that make you want to stay; the whole thing is one slow mouth.
pressures: HARM (find the heart in the mass)
roster.clean: Growth is not always good. This one grows to eat. Burning it back is the garden's mercy.

roster.name: the Ashen Wyrm
roster.look: A dragon of the death-pole — hill-sized, ash-scaled, its breath the grey stillness of everything stopping at once. Where it flies, the season ends. The Ashwardens' mercy given wings and turned to a weather.
roster.danger: Its breath stops craft and slows blood across a valley; a wingbeat is a wind of endings; it does not hunt, it PASSES, and what it passes over is done.
pressures: UNMAKE (the only thing that touches it)
roster.clean: A dragon is a domain that forgot everything but appetite. This one's appetite is endings. It cannot be reasoned with because there is no it — only the death-pole, flying. Ending it is the largest mercy the valley will ever be asked to give.
roster.epicNote: Domain-scale. Not a fight — a campaign (ties SNG-208 offscreen-epic/arc). A growing world-threat; slaying it is a saga, not an encounter.

roster.name: the Bright Devourer
roster.look: A dragon of the light-pole — scales like struck glass, a radiance that permits no shadow and no secret. It does not burn; it REVEALS, and what it reveals it consumes. The Blazeborn truth given wings and gone starving.
roster.danger: Its light strips cover, illusion, and hidden craft for miles; you fight it with nowhere to hide, everything you are laid bare; the revelation itself is the weapon.
pressures: SWAY (hold your self against the stripping light)
roster.clean: Truth that devours what it shows. There is no one behind the light — only the light-pole, hungry. To end it is to let the world keep its shadows, which is to say, keep its secrets, which is to say, keep itself.
roster.epicNote: Domain-scale. A campaign, not a fight. Antipode of the Ashen Wyrm — the two dragons are the death/life... no, dark/light poles given wing. (SNG-208 arc-scale threat.)

roster.name: the Unspooling Worm
roster.look: A dragon of the destruction-pole — vast, segmented, wingless, boring through the world itself; where it passes, made things come UNMADE, back to the raw material they were built from. The Unmakers' ethic of clearing, given a body the size of a river and no ethic left.
roster.danger: Unmakes structure — walls, bindings, crafts, the ground — in a wake behind it; you cannot fortify against it, only outmaneuver and strike the one moving thing.
roster.clean: Clearing with nothing left to clear FOR. It unmakes because unmaking is all that remains of what it was. Ending it lets the made things stay made.

roster.name: the narrowed
roster.look: A body still doing the last thing it was told, long after the telling stopped mattering. It is not rotting — the rot is being used. The face is the part that went first.
roster.danger: It does not tire, does not fear, and does not stop. ⛔ A MENDING LAID ON IT BURNS IT: the same vitality that closes a living wound is the thing it has been emptied of. ⚠️ And it is untouched by anything aimed at a self — terror, grief, a true name, a named reckoning all pass through the space where the person was.
pressures: RESTORE (a mending is a weapon here)
UNMAKE (end the errand, not the body)
KNOW (read which raising it came from)
HARM (heat and edge still work, slowly)
roster.clean: It finishes the motion it was in, and then it is a body.
roster._authored_20260829: ⛔ ERIK 2026-08-29: 'HEALING WILL NEED TO BE TYPED — we've moved past that original idea, IT CAN HURT UNDEAD NOW.' ⚠️ THE RULING NEEDED A CREATURE OR IT WAS THEORETICAL: the bestiary had 26 entries and NOT ONE UNDEAD, so §48's whole undeath model had nothing to run on. ✅ THIS ENTRY CARRIES BOTH HALVES OF THE INVERSION AND NEEDS NO NEW MACHINERY: `decay: absorb` (already works — absorb returns negative damage, so rot mends it) and `vitality: vulnerable` (works NOW, because healing crafts carry a type as of today). ⛔ A `heal` lands on it through the ordinary damage path and hurts. ⚠️ `feeling: immune` IS THE SAME BLIND SPOT `break_the_line` AND `the_known_name` DECLARE — nothing without a self can be frightened, which is why a Marcher's terror and an Ashwarden's driven dead are natural counters to each other. ⛔ NARROWED, NOT AN AFTERLING: the design laws exclude persons from the bestiary, and an Afterling is a person. This is the end state that ISN'T.
roster._feelingRemoved_20260830: ⛔ `feeling: immune` REMOVED, AND THAT IS THE FIX — NOT ADDING IT TO THE OTHER SEVEN SELFLESS CREATURES. ⚠️ I OWED 'creatures that should declare it and do not' and the answer turned out to be the opposite of what I expected: `hasSelf: false` on the CLASS now does this job for every selfless creature at once, through `selfBlocked`. ✅ CCode's own note is the argument: 'THE CLASS IS RESOLVED, NEVER STORED ON THE SHEET — a copied `hasSelf` would be a stored copy of a derived value, WHICH IS THE FAILURE THIS PROJECT HAS COMMITTED MOST.' ⛔ MY `feeling: immune` WAS EXACTLY THAT COPY, written before the property existed. Adding seven more would have put one fact in nine places. ⚠️ WHAT IS LOST AND WHY IT IS ACCEPTABLE: `feeling: immune` also blocked feeling DAMAGE from a craft that does not declare `requiresSelf` — e.g. `grief_strike`. That is a real question (should grief wound a thing with no self?) and it belongs to `requiresSelf` on those crafts, not to a per-creature flag on one of eight.

roster.name: the gathering
roster.look: ⛔ NOTHING IS THERE AND THE SPACE IS OCCUPIED. A cold that pools where a floor is level. Breath that hangs a half-second too long. ⚠️ IT IS SEEN BY WHAT IT HAS TAKEN — the animals gone from a valley, the well that stopped, a room where nobody will sit. Where it has fed long enough there is a shape to it, thin and unfinished, wearing pieces of the endings it ate: a posture, a favoured hand, the way somebody used to stand. ⛔ NONE OF THOSE ARE ITS OWN.
roster.danger: ⛔ IT GETS STRONGER AND IT NEVER STOPS. Every ending that goes unattended within its reach is taken up — not the person, who is already gone, but WHAT WAS LEFT UNFINISHED IN THE CROSSING. ⚠️ A well-attended country starves it. A battlefield nobody walked, a plague nobody sat with, a road where people die alone — it thickens on those. ⛔ A MENDING LAID ON IT BURNS IT, the same inversion as the narrowed. ⚠️ AND IT IS UNTOUCHED BY ANYTHING AIMED AT A SELF: terror, a true name, a named reckoning all pass through, because the postures it wears were borrowed and there is nobody behind them.
pressures: KNOW (⛔ THE HARD PART IS FINDING IT — it is a place that is wrong before it is a thing that is there)
RESTORE (a mending is a weapon here)
UNMAKE (⚠️ scatter what it has gathered; the pieces do not reassemble into anyone)
WARD (⛔ THE REAL COUNTER — attend the endings in its reach and it starves. Slow, and it is the only cure)
roster.clean: ⚠️ IT DOES NOT DIE, IT DISPERSES. What it had gathered lets go at once — a room's worth of unfinished endings arriving all together, which is not violent and is very hard to be present for.
roster._authored_20260902: ⛔ ERIK 2026-09-02: 'I DO want a creature that gets stronger and feeds off of unattended deaths.' ⚠️ IT IS THE DIRECT CONSEQUENCE OF R29 — if attending preserves personhood across the crossing, then an unattended ending LEAVES SOMETHING BEHIND, and this is what eats it. ✅ NO NEW MACHINERY: `decay: absorb` and `vitality: vulnerable` carry §48's inversion exactly as `the_narrowed` does. ⛔ AND IT IS NOT AN AFTERLING AND NEVER BECOMES ONE — the design laws exclude persons, and this has no self, no want, and no grievance. It wears postures it took and there is nobody behind them. ⚠️ THE WARD PRESSURE IS THE POINT: the counter is not a fight, it is a TRADITION DOING ITS JOB. An Ashwarden who attends the endings in a valley starves it out over months. ➡️ That makes `the_attended_end` matter at world scale and gives 22 non-striking traditions a way in, per design law 3.
roster._notTheStillwaterThing: ⬜ THIS IS NOT THE THING UNDER STILLWATER'S TROUBLE. Erik left that unruled ('I'm not sure about the thing under the post'). ⚠️ This is a CLASS that exists in the world; that is a specific, and it is still open.

roster.name: the Standing Legion
roster.look: A whole army, dead since before the Transition, still holding the line it was ordered to hold. Four thousand of them across a valley floor, shields up, facing an enemy that stopped existing centuries ago. They do not rot. They do not move until something crosses the line.
roster.danger: Anything that crosses the line is the enemy. They answer as an army answers — in ranks, in volleys, by the thousand — and they do not tire, break or rout. A road that runs through their valley is closed.
pressures: KNOW (find the order they are still obeying)
SHAPE (give them a true ending to the war)
roster.clean: Not four thousand people — one order, still running in four thousand bodies. There is no one in there to grieve. Ending it is telling the war it is over.
roster._why: A legendary that a strong party cannot simply fight: the answer is to read the order and end it. The class's own concept (a body still doing the last thing it was told) scaled to an army.

roster.name: the Ninefold Foundry
roster.look: A pre-Transition foundry the size of a town, woken and walking on legs it built for itself out of its own furnaces. It is still making things. It has been making them for a very long time, and none of them are for anyone.
roster.danger: It takes whatever it walks over as stock — stone, iron, a hold's walls, the people inside — and it makes something out of it. What it makes then works for it, until it is taken apart for stock in turn.
pressures: KNOW (read what it thinks it is building)
SHAPE (finish the project, so it stops)
roster.clean: A tool with no hand left to hold it, following an order that no longer means anything. Stopping it is repair by other means.
roster._why: The feral_construct class at legendary scale. The Gearfather (heroic) is its small cousin, so the class climbs the ladder.

roster.name: the Eye of the Storm
roster.look: Where the Manifestation Storm is thickest, the air thinks. It is not a creature. It is a place that dreams creatures, a sky that keeps almost-becoming something and then does, briefly, before it forgets.
roster.danger: Whatever it dreams walks out of it. Its thoughts become weather, and its weather becomes things with teeth. Standing inside it is standing inside a mind that does not know you are there, and it may think you into something else.
pressures: KNOW (read a thought the size of a sky)
roster.clean: No one is there to kill. It is the Storm's own centre — ending it is calming weather, and the grief is for everything it could have made.
roster._why: Mythic, and unique in the world: the Storm arc's own heart, met as an ending rather than a roll on a road. The world's biggest version of the Unmoored Choir (epic).

roster.name: the First Root
roster.look: A forest that is one living thing, the size of a region. Every tree in it is the same tree. Its roots run under three traditions' lands, and it has been growing, very slowly, toward something no one has understood.
roster.danger: It does not attack. It grows. A hold on its edge wakes one morning inside it, and the road home has become a root. The things that live inside it are its hands, and it has a great many hands.
pressures: KNOW (find what it is growing toward)
WARD (keep a place from being taken in)
MOVE (find a way through a forest that moves)
UNMAKE (at a cost to the land itself)
roster.clean: A growth, not a grievance. It wants nothing but to grow. Stopping it is the Green Schism's hardest question: what is taken from the living world to keep the human one.
roster._why: Mythic, unique, and tied to the Green Schism, so ending it is an arc choice rather than a kill. The Bloom That Hungers (heroic) is its seed.

roster.name: corpse-lights
roster.look: Pale lamps bobbing low over black water, always a little ahead, always the same distance away. They look like someone carrying a lantern home.
roster.danger: They lead. Follow them and the ground goes soft, then goes under. They do not bite; the marsh does.
pressures: KNOW (see that no one holds the lamp)
WARD (keep your feet on firm ground)
MOVE (turn back the way you came)
roster.storyRule: The Ashwarden children's rule: a light that will not let you catch up is not going home. Walk away from it and it forgets you.
roster.clean: Nothing to kill. Snuff the light and there is only swamp gas and the sound of frogs.

roster.name: a pack of grave-eaters
roster.look: Long-armed, grey-skinned things that move on all fours between the stones, faces pressed to the earth. Their nails are black with it.
roster.danger: They dig up what the Ashwardens laid down and they are not particular about whether it has finished dying. Their claws numb; a scratched limb goes slow and cold.
pressures: MOVE (they are quick in the dark)
roster.storyRule: Every Ashwarden grandmother's story: they cannot cross a line of ash laid with a prayer. The old grave-rings still work.
roster.clean: The story that made them was told to keep children out of graveyards. Ending them keeps the dead where they were put.

roster.name: a barrow-wight
roster.look: A tall shape in rotted mail at the mouth of an old barrow, crowned with a band of dull gold. Its breath frosts in summer. Its eyes are two cold sparks.
roster.danger: Its touch drinks warmth: fingers, then hands, then the will to move. It guards the barrow's gold and anything that takes a coin from it is followed home.
pressures: HARM (break the crown, not the body)
roster.storyRule: Put back what was taken, every coin, and it lies down again. The story says it was only ever a guard who was never relieved.
roster.clean: A duty that outlived its keeper. Relieve it and there is only old bone and cold gold.

roster.name: a snare-vine thicket
roster.look: A green wall of creeper that is slightly too thick, slightly too still, and has a boot in it.
roster.danger: It closes. Slowly, then not slowly. Whatever it holds long enough becomes part of the thicket.
roster.storyRule: The Rootkin say ask it to open. Speak to it as you would to a garden and it loosens; hack at it and it grips.
roster.clean: A plant that learned hunting from a story. Burn it back and the wood grows normal green in its place.

roster.name: a briar-bear
roster.look: A bear the size of a cart with an owl's great round face and a hide grown through with thorned briar. It hoots before it charges, low, like a question.
roster.danger: It mauls. The briar tears whatever the claws miss, and it does not stop for wounds; it stops when you are not moving.
roster.storyRule: The Rootkin tale: it only hunts what runs. Stand still and answer the hoot with a hoot, and it will circle, puzzled, and go.
roster.clean: Half a bear, half a bedtime story told to keep children out of the deep wood. Put down, it is a bear again, and very old.

roster.name: a nest of weaver-spiders
roster.look: Webs strung tree to tree like sails, and in them spiders the size of dogs, patient and many-eyed and nearly beautiful.
roster.danger: Poison that slows the limbs, webs that hold like rope, and more of them than there seemed to be.
roster.storyRule: Fire, the old story says, and the story is right. Their silk burns fast and they will not follow through smoke.
roster.clean: Spiders a frightened people made too big. The wood is better with smaller ones.

roster.name: a shambling mound
roster.look: A heap of rotting vegetation the height of a man and a half, which stands up. Things are tangled in it. Some of them were travellers.
roster.danger: It enfolds. It smothers and digests slowly, and blades sink into it and come out wet. Lightning, the story says, only feeds it.
roster.storyRule: It cannot leave wet ground. Draw it onto dry stone and it slows, then crumbles.
roster.clean: The marsh's hunger with a shape put on it. Scatter it and it is only compost.

roster.name: a heartwood colossus
roster.look: An oak that walks, three storeys high, bark split with old axe-scars, moss for a beard. There is no face in it anymore, only the place where one was.
roster.danger: It was woken to guard a grove and the grove is long gone. It guards the ground now, from everything, and its roots come up under your feet.
pressures: KNOW (find what it thinks it is guarding)
SHAPE (give it a grove to keep)
roster.storyRule: Plant something in its sight and it stops to guard the seedling. The Rootkin do this still, on purpose.
roster.clean: A guardian with nothing left to guard. Ending it is felling an old tree. Giving it a sapling is kinder, and it works.

roster.name: a nest of salamanders
roster.look: Red-gold lizards the length of an arm, basking in a vent where the rock glows. The air shimmers. Their tongues are flame.
roster.danger: They set what they touch alight, and they come out in numbers when the nest is disturbed.
roster.storyRule: Every Blazeborn smith knows: they will not leave the heat. Step off the warm stone and they will not follow.
roster.clean: Sparks that got legs in a forge-story. Put out, they are only ash and a smell of pitch.

roster.name: a brace of pyre-hounds
roster.look: Two long black dogs with coals for eyes and smoke curling from their jaws, trotting just off the road, keeping pace.
roster.danger: They run their quarry down and their bite burns. The grass behind them smoulders for a day.
roster.storyRule: The Blazeborn road-tale says they hunt only the oathbreaker. Keep a promise in your mouth, spoken aloud, and they pass you by.
roster.clean: The story of the hound that punishes a broken oath, grown teeth. End them and the road is only a road.

roster.name: a cinder wyvern
roster.look: A lean two-legged dragon-kin with leather wings the colour of banked coals and a barbed tail that drips something that hisses on stone.
roster.danger: It stoops from height, rakes, and climbs again. The tail's sting burns inside the wound for days.
roster.storyRule: It cannot land on wet ground; the smiths' story says it fears the quench. Water on its roost drives it off for a season.
roster.clean: A drake out of a forge-song, not a true dragon and not a person. The mountain is quieter without it.

roster.name: darkmantles
roster.look: Something like a black cloak hanging from the ceiling of the passage. Then several somethings. Then they drop.
roster.danger: They fall on the head, wrap it and squeeze, and they snuff every light near them as they come.
roster.storyRule: The Umbral miners' rule: a lit passage has no mantles. They only hang where the dark has been left alone for a year.
roster.clean: Shadows a nervous people gave weight to. Pinned in the light, they curl up like burnt paper.

roster.name: a shade-panther
roster.look: A great black cat with two long whip-tendrils from its shoulders, and it is never quite where it seems to be. You strike where it is and it is a pace to the left.
roster.danger: It hunts by misdirection: the image it throws is where your blow goes, and the tendrils come from somewhere else.
roster.storyRule: Close one eye, the Umbral hunters say. The shadow it throws only fools two eyes at once.
roster.clean: A hunting cat from a story about the dark lying to you. Killed, it is exactly where it lies.

roster.name: the grue
roster.look: No one has seen it. That is the point. There is a breathing in the unlit passage, and a smell like wet iron, and then there is not you.
roster.danger: It eats those who walk without light. That is all the story says, and the story is exact.
pressures: WARD (never let your light go out)
UNMAKE (bring the dark to an end)
roster.storyRule: The whole rule is in the story: it cannot abide light. Keep a flame and you are safe. Lose it and you are likely to be eaten.
roster.clean: Nothing to see and nothing to kill. Light the passage and it is only a passage.

roster.name: bargain-mites
roster.look: Tiny red things like winged beetles that settle on the shoulder and whisper in the ear. They smell of warm coins.
roster.danger: They offer. Small things, easy things: sleep, a better price, a friend's secret. Every yes feeds them and every one costs a little more than it said.
roster.storyRule: The Bargainers' first lesson: say no three times, aloud. A mite that hears three refusals falls off dead.
roster.clean: Temptations with wings. There is no one in them, only the offer.

roster.name: a hellhound pack
roster.look: Rust-red hounds with brimstone breath and eyes like lamp-glass, baying at a pitch that sets teeth on edge.
roster.danger: They breathe fire in short gouts and hunt by the scent of broken bargains. The baying makes the bravest want to run.
pressures: KNOW (what they have been sent after)
roster.storyRule: They will not cross running water; every abyssal story agrees on that.
roster.clean: A debt-collector's dogs from a story about unpaid debts. Ended, they leave a smell of sulphur and a lighter road.

roster.name: a mimic
roster.look: A strongbox, iron-bound and slightly open, with the glint of coin inside. Or a door. Or a chair. It is whatever you were hoping to find.
roster.danger: It bites whoever reaches for it and the bite sticks: an adhesive hide that holds the hand while the lid comes down.
roster.storyRule: The Bargainers' saying: never take a thing that is exactly what you wanted. Tap it with a stick first.
roster.clean: A lesson about greed with a mouth. Killed, it is only a lumpy grey thing, and there was never any gold.

roster.name: halo-moths
roster.look: White moths with wings like hammered gold leaf, circling a lamp that is not there. Their light is very bright and very judging.
roster.danger: They blind. The light shows every shameful thing you have done to everyone who can see it, and for a moment you believe it too.
roster.storyRule: A clear conscience, the Orders say, and they pass. Confess something true aloud and the swarm breaks.
roster.clean: A sermon about being seen, given wings. There is no judgment in them; they only reflect.

roster.name: a griffon pair
roster.look: Eagle-headed lions the size of horses, gold-feathered at the neck, nesting on a cliff above the road. They watch everything that passes.
roster.danger: They drop on horses and pack animals first, then on whoever defends them. The beak goes through mail.
pressures: SHAPE (feed them, and they may let you pass)
roster.storyRule: The Orders' tale says the griffon guards the honest traveller's gold. Carry nothing stolen and they only watch.
roster.clean: The standard of an order become a beast. They are majestic, and they will eat your horse.

roster.name: a sphinx
roster.look: A lion's body the size of a house, lying across a gateway, with a face of carved serenity and eyes that follow you. It speaks, but only one thing.
roster.danger: It asks the riddle. Answer and pass. Answer wrong and it eats you. It cannot be talked to, bargained with or begged; it only knows the question.
roster.storyRule: The Orders' tale ends with the one who answered correctly and the sphinx that lay down and slept. It keeps the rule it was made with.
roster.clean: Not a person: a gate that asks. Answered, it sleeps. Killed, it is a great stone lion with nothing behind its eyes.

roster.name: a gargoyle roost
roster.look: Carved grotesques along a cornice, open-mouthed, winged, weathered. One of them has moved since you last looked.
roster.danger: They come down at dusk on stone wings and they are stone all through. They do not bleed and they do not tire.
roster.storyRule: The Masons carve them to keep something else away. They sleep in daylight, and a Mason's mark cut on the doorstep turns them.
roster.clean: Watchers a building-people imagined into waking. Broken, they are only rubble with faces.

roster.name: an empty suit of armor on watch
roster.look: Full plate standing at a post, halberd grounded, visor down. The helm is empty. It has been on watch for longer than the post has stood.
roster.danger: It challenges anyone who passes without the word, and it fights with the patience of a thing that cannot be hurt in the places people are hurt.
roster.storyRule: Give it the watchword or relieve it formally, and it stands down.
roster.clean: An order to stand guard, still standing guard. Relieved, it falls apart into a heap of old metal.

roster.name: a stone golem
roster.look: Twice a man's height, cut from a single grey block, a word chiselled on its brow. It moves like a millstone: slowly, and then it has arrived.
roster.danger: It strikes like falling masonry and nothing ordinary hurts it. It keeps its maker's last instruction, whatever that was.
roster.storyRule: Every Mason story: scratch out one letter of the word and it is only stone.
roster.clean: A made servant with no maker left. Stopping it is repair by other means.

roster.name: clockwork spiders
roster.look: A skitter of brass spiders the size of a hand, ticking, each with one red lens. They repair what they find and they are not particular about what counts as broken.
roster.danger: They swarm and snip and solder. They take apart gear, packs, and ankles with equal interest.
roster.storyRule: The Enginewrights' saying: find the key. There is always a master spider with a winding key in its back, and stopping it stops the rest.
roster.clean: A tool-story with no hands to answer to. Stopped, they are a pile of beautiful brass.

roster.name: a rust-eater
roster.look: Something like a hairless insect-dog with two feathered antennae, sniffing. It is interested in your belt buckle. It is very interested in your sword.
roster.danger: Its antennae rust any metal they touch to flakes in a heartbeat. It is not dangerous to you so much as to everything you own.
pressures: HARM (with wood, stone or a bare hand)
SHAPE (throw it something else to eat)
roster.storyRule: The smiths' joke: carry an iron nail to throw. It always chases the nearer meal.
roster.clean: A metalworker's nightmare that came true. It isn't cruel, only hungry, and entirely unwelcome.

roster.name: an iron colossus
roster.look: A pre-Transition war machine in the shape of a giant, forty feet of iron plate and pipes, standing in a crater it made. When it wakes, the ground knows first.
roster.danger: Its fists level walls. It vents a poison vapour when pressed, and it answers to an army that no longer exists.
pressures: KNOW (find the command it's waiting for)
roster.storyRule: The oldest Enginewright tale: every colossus was built with a word to stop it. The word is somewhere in the ruin it guards.
roster.clean: A weapon from a war nobody remembers, still waiting for orders. Ending it is disarmament.

roster.name: a perfect cube
roster.look: A cube of perfectly clear jelly exactly the width of the passage, moving along it at a walking pace. There are bones in it, a helmet, a few coins, all neatly spaced.
roster.danger: It engulfs and digests. Anything it touches is paralysed first, then taken in, and it cleans the corridor behind it to a shine.
roster.storyRule: The Syllogists' puzzle: it is a perfect cube, so it cannot turn a corner. Take a side passage and wait.
roster.clean: A logician's idea of tidiness made solid. There is nothing in it but its rule.

roster.name: a face-thief
roster.look: Someone you know, standing where they should not be, smiling slightly wrong. Up close their eyes do not blink at the same time.
roster.danger: It wears the face of someone you trust and leads you somewhere quiet. What is behind the face is not a person; it is only hunger shaped like a friend.
pressures: KNOW (ask something only they would know)
roster.storyRule: The Verist rule: ask it to say something false. It cannot. It can only repeat what it has heard.
roster.clean: The story of the stranger with a friend's face, made real and empty. Ended, it has no face at all.

roster.name: the hounds of the angled hour
roster.look: Lean grey things that come out of the corners of a room, where the walls meet at a sharp angle. They look starved. They smell of old dust and burnt clocks.
roster.danger: They hunt anyone who has meddled with time, across any distance, through any sharp corner. They do not stop.
pressures: MOVE (to a place with no corners)
roster.storyRule: The Hourkeepers plaster their rooms round. The hounds can only come through an angle less than a right angle, and a curved room has none.
roster.clean: The Hourkeepers' warning to their apprentices, now with teeth. Take away their corners and they are gone.

roster.name: lattice-crawlers
roster.look: Glass insects in a glittering swarm, each one a perfect little prism, marching in rank across a wall and breaking the light into colours.
roster.danger: They cut. A swarm across the skin is a thousand tiny facets, and they grow the more light they catch.
roster.storyRule: Lattice children learn it: cover the lamp. In the dark they stop and wait for day.
roster.clean: Geometry with legs, from a city that dreamed in prisms. Crushed, they are sand.

roster.name: a siren shoal
roster.look: Singing, from the rocks at the river's bend. When you look there are only seals, or women, or something with too many teeth, depending on who looks.
roster.danger: The song pulls. Those who hear it walk toward the water and keep walking, and the shoal takes whoever reaches them.
pressures: WARD (stop your ears, or your heart)
roster.storyRule: The Threnodists sing back. A true song of grief sung louder drowns theirs, and they go quiet to listen.
roster.clean: Mourning songs that learned to lure. Ended, the rocks are only rocks, and the river sounds like a river.

roster.name: a harpy flock
roster.look: Vulture-winged, taloned, screaming things with faces a little too human, wheeling above a cliff road and a litter of stripped packs.
roster.danger: They dive to snatch food, gear, anything shiny, and they shriek in a voice that makes the listener feel every grief at once.
roster.storyRule: Leave something for them and they fight each other over it instead of you. Every Threnodist on that road carries a loaf to throw.
roster.clean: Grief given wings in a sad people's songs. Driven off, the cliff is only a cliff.

roster.name: a glamour-fox
roster.look: A fox with a tail that trails a faint shimmer, sitting at a fork in the road that was not there yesterday.
roster.danger: It makes paths. Follow one and you walk for an hour and come back to the fox, who is grinning. Some travellers never come back to it.
roster.storyRule: Turn your coat inside out, the Veilwrights say. The glamour holds only on what faces it.
roster.clean: A trickster story with a fox's body. Caught, it is only a fox, and rather embarrassed.

roster.name: a blink-hound pack
roster.look: Yellow-furred hounds that are here, and then there, with a small pop of air, and then behind you.
roster.danger: They attack from everywhere at once because they are everywhere at once. Fleeing does not work; they are already where you are running to.
roster.storyRule: They cannot blink into a place already full. The Horizon-Walkers stand in a tight ring, backs together.
roster.clean: A story about how nothing is far away any more. They are not cruel; they are dogs who can step between places.

roster.name: a phase spider
roster.look: A spider the size of a pony, pale and faintly transparent, that steps out of nothing beside you, bites, and steps back into nothing.
roster.danger: Its bite is a deep poison and it is never there to be struck. It strikes from outside the world and returns to it.
pressures: HARM (in the instant it is here)
roster.storyRule: Iron nailed across a threshold, the old way-lore says, keeps the between shut. It cannot step through iron.
roster.clean: A spider that learned the trick of the waygates. Closed out, it is only a spider in a place it cannot leave.

roster.name: churn-rats
roster.look: Rats, but each of them wrong in a different way: this one with a lizard's tail, that one with feathers, one with far too many eyes.
roster.danger: They breed fast, eat everything, and carry sickness from whatever they were mixed with.
pressures: HARM (they die easily, one at a time)
roster.storyRule: Salt. The Churnfolk say a ring of salt holds a shape still, and a churn-rat inside it becomes only a rat.
roster.clean: What the churn does to vermin. Ended, the cellar is only a cellar.

roster.name: a chimera
roster.look: A lion's forebody, a goat's head rising from its back, a serpent for a tail. Each head has its own eyes and they do not agree about where to look.
roster.danger: Three heads, three minds, three attacks: the lion bites, the goat breathes fire, the serpent strikes from behind.
roster.storyRule: The Churnfolk riddle-answer: make the heads argue. Offer each a different prize and it turns on itself.
roster.clean: The churn's favourite story: a beast made of three beasts. Ended, it falls apart into the animals it was stitched from.

roster.name: a marsh hydra
roster.look: Seven necks rising out of the reeds, each ending in a snake's head the size of a man's torso. Cut one and two grow.
roster.danger: It bites from seven directions and regrows what is cut, and the fens it lives in are its own flooded ground.
roster.storyRule: The oldest story has the answer: sear each neck as it is cut. Fire stops the regrowing.
roster.clean: The churn's idea of never ending. Ended, it is only a great drowned snake, and the fen can be drained.

roster.name: a bridge-troll
roster.look: Something huge and warty and green-grey living under the bridge, with long arms and a long nose, and bones in the water around its feet.
roster.danger: It demands the toll and eats whoever cannot pay. Every wound it takes closes as you watch.
pressures: HARM (with fire, so it cannot heal)
roster.storyRule: The Somatic tale says it regrows anything but a burn. And it is so proud of its body it will stop to wrestle anyone who dares it.
roster.clean: The body that will not stop healing, from a people who worship the body. Burned, it stays down.

roster.name: a cockatrice
roster.look: A rooster the size of a dog with a serpent's tail and a mad red eye. Around its roost, a scatter of small stone animals.
roster.danger: Its peck turns flesh to stone, slowly, from the wound outward.
pressures: KNOW (how far the stone has spread)
roster.storyRule: The Figurists draw a weasel. The pattern of the one animal it fears, chalked on the barn door, keeps it off.
roster.clean: A farmyard nightmare. Killed, it is only a big, ugly bird, and the stone animals do not come back.

roster.name: a basilisk
roster.look: A great eight-legged lizard with a heavy crowned head, basking among statues of the people who came to kill it.
roster.danger: Meet its gaze and you are stone. It does not even need to try; it only has to look at you.
roster.storyRule: Every Figurist knows the pattern completes itself: show it its own eyes in a mirror and it turns itself to stone.
roster.clean: A story about the danger of being seen. Ended, it is a lizard, and the statues are still statues.

roster.name: a burrow-shark
roster.look: A fin cutting through dry earth like water, and then a great armoured head bursting up out of the ground with a mouth like a well.
roster.danger: It hunts by the tremor of feet. It swallows horses. It leaves the ground behind it churned and dangerous.
pressures: HARM (under the crest, when it leaps)
roster.storyRule: It cannot dig through bedrock. The Unmakers' frontier farms stand on stone shelves for a reason.
roster.clean: The earth itself hungry, in an Unmaker story. Killed, it is an armoured beast in a trench.

roster.name: a delving worm
roster.look: A purple-black worm as wide as a road, rising out of a new tunnel with a round mouth full of teeth in rings. Its tail carries a sting the length of a man.
roster.danger: It swallows whole, it stings with a poison that kills, and it leaves a tunnel behind it that other things come out of.
roster.storyRule: The Unmakers say it cannot bear a true silence. Everyone stops. Everyone holds still. It loses you.
roster.clean: The ground's appetite in a story about unmaking. The tunnels it leaves become roads, eventually.

roster.name: tool-imps
roster.look: A workshop full of little clay-and-wire figures the size of a thumb, busily improving things. They have improved the door hinges. They have improved the lamp oil.
roster.danger: They make things better, by their own measure. A cart with better wheels that go their own way; a sword with a better edge that cuts its owner.
roster.storyRule: The Wrights' fix: give them a job. A tool-imp with work to do does that work and nothing else.
roster.clean: A maker's fancy about helpers, given hands. Stopped, they are clay and wire.

roster.name: a dire wolf pack
roster.look: Wolves the size of ponies, grey-white, running silent over snow with their breath smoking. The leader's muzzle is scarred to the bone.
roster.danger: They take stragglers and horses and they are patient enough to follow for days.
roster.storyRule: The Marchers light a ring of fires and wait for dawn. The pack will not cross fire, and they go at first light.
roster.clean: The frontier's hunger in the Marchers' winter tales. Only wolves, but very large ones.

roster.name: a frontier wyvern
roster.look: A grey, scale-armoured flier with a wingspan like a sail and a stinging tail, circling over the border posts at dusk.
roster.danger: It takes cattle, horses, sentries. The tail's poison stops the heart.
roster.storyRule: The border posts have a horn for it. A long low note makes it think another wyvern holds this ground, and it goes elsewhere.
roster.clean: The border's fear with wings. Driven off, it is only a beast, hungry, somewhere else.

roster.name: a snow-ape troop
roster.look: Shaggy white apes, taller than a man, moving on their knuckles across a snowfield so quietly the snow does not creak.
roster.danger: They ambush in blizzards, throw boulders from ledges, and carry off the ones who fall behind.
roster.storyRule: The Stillhold's rule for the high passes: never cross in a storm. They only hunt when they cannot be seen.
roster.clean: The silence of the snow given shape. Ended, it is only an animal, very large, very cold.

roster.name: a frost worm
roster.look: A pale blue worm the length of three wagons, lying coiled in the snow. As it rises, its back glows red-hot where the plates part.
roster.danger: Its back burns anything that touches it and its keening freezes the listener where they stand.
roster.storyRule: Stop your ears with wax, the Stillhold says. The song freezes only those who hear it.
roster.clean: Cold and heat together, a riddle from a still people. Killed, it leaves a patch of melted snow that never refreezes.

roster.name: a leech-eel run
roster.look: Black eels as long as an arm running upstream in a writhing mass, and the water turns dark where they pass.
roster.danger: They latch and drain. A wader comes out of the river pale and shaking with half a dozen of them on each leg.
roster.storyRule: Salt on the skin, every river-story says. They drop off at once and do not come back.
roster.clean: A ford-story that grew teeth. Only eels, and hungry.

roster.name: a kelpie
roster.look: A beautiful grey horse standing in the shallows, saddled and bridled, looking at you with calm dark eyes. Its mane is wet. Its mane is always wet.
roster.danger: Mount it and you cannot get off. It walks into the river and down and does not come up.
pressures: KNOW (see the weed in its mane)
roster.storyRule: Take its bridle and it must serve you, the stories say. Never mount it before you have the bridle.
roster.clean: The river's beauty and its danger in one shape. Ended, it is river-weed and water.

roster.name: a stirge cloud
roster.look: A cloud of rust-brown things like mosquitoes the size of sparrows, with long needle noses, rising from the reeds at dusk.
roster.danger: Each one drinks. Dozens at once drink a lot.
roster.storyRule: Smoke. Every traveller's story says it. A smoky fire keeps them off the camp.
roster.clean: The marsh's thirst in a cloud. Only insects, very large ones.

roster.name: a roc
roster.look: A shadow crosses the whole valley and the light goes grey. Overhead, an eagle with a wingspan wider than a village carries off a cow.
roster.danger: It takes oxen, horses, people, and drops what it doesn't want from a great height.
roster.storyRule: It will not take anything that is under a roof. Every story about the roc is a story about going inside.
roster.clean: The great bird of every people's sky-stories. Only a bird, the biggest one there is.

roster.name: the ash-and-ember bird
roster.look: A bird of fire the size of a barn, trailing embers, crossing the sky at dusk. Everything it flies over catches.
roster.danger: It burns whatever it lands on. It cannot be killed: it burns to ash and rises from the ash, larger. Each time it rises, a season's worth of land burns with it.
roster.storyRule: The Blazeborn's oldest story: it rises only from its own ash. Scatter the ash on running water and it does not come back.
roster.clean: A people's story about renewal, at a scale that burns forests. Ending it is choosing which renewal the land can survive.
roster.epicNote: A campaign, not a fight. It can't be killed by harm alone; the answer is its own story.

roster.name: the deep kraken
roster.look: Tentacles rising out of the deep water beside the ship, each thicker than the mast, and between them an eye the size of a door.
roster.danger: It takes ships. It wraps and pulls down, and the harbour it lives beneath is a place no one sails any more.
roster.storyRule: Every harbour story agrees: it rises only to the sound of oars. The old sailors come in under sail, in silence.
roster.clean: The deep water's fear with arms. Ending it gives a harbour back to its people.

roster.name: the Wakeful Beast
roster.look: The story every people tells about the thing at the end of the world, and it is true: a scaled, horned beast the size of a hill, asleep under a plateau, with a slow breath that shakes the valley once a year.
roster.danger: When it wakes it walks, and it eats, and there is no army, city or hold that stops it. Nothing wounds it faster than it heals.
pressures: UNMAKE (at the cost of a tradition's whole craft)
roster.storyRule: Every story ends the same way: it was never killed, only put back to sleep. The lullaby is split between the peoples; each one knows a verse.
roster.clean: The shared nightmare of every tradition. Ending it is the one thing all the peoples would have to do together.
roster.epicNote: Mythic, unique. Never rolled. Met through the peoples' shared arc: the verses of the lullaby are a quest across every tradition.

roster.name: an arch-warden
roster.look: A figure made of the gate's own stone, grey and seamless, the lattice lines glowing faintly along where its joints should be. It steps out of the arch and stands there, facing whoever holds it, and does not blink because it has nothing to blink with.
roster.danger: It walks to the nearest of the holder's people at the gate and puts them out of the yard, not gently. If they come back it does it again, harder. Two or three of them can hold a gatehouse empty for a day.
pressures: WARD (hold the arch against a thing made of it)
KNOW (read what it was sent to do)
roster.storyRule: They leave when the gate is released. Take down the banner, open the arch, stop charging for passage, and whatever came through goes back through it within the day. Every people tells some version of this; the Crossing's porters say it to every new lord who looks at the Hub Yard too long.
roster.clean: The network keeping itself. Nobody sent it and nobody is in it. Releasing the gate is the whole answer.
roster._why: SNG-663 Â§2c. Never on a random table: a keeper comes only for whoever holds a gate, on the escalation clock (notable, heroic, epic, legendary, a season apart), and stops when the gate is released.

roster.name: the threshold choir
roster.look: A ring of light that stands in the arch and sings, one sustained chord in a key the lattice lines answer to. Anyone standing under the arch hears it inside their teeth. The stones of the yard begin to ring in sympathy.
roster.danger: The chord unmakes what the holder has built at the gate: bars, gatehouses, the chains across the arch, the toll-board. People are not its target, but they are standing inside it. A garrison that stays through a full verse comes out deaf, or doesn't come out.
pressures: WARD (keep your shape inside a note)
SHAPE (answer it in its own key)
UNMAKE (the chord, at a cost to the arch)

Every people tells some version of this; the Crossing's porters say it to every new lord who looks at the Hub Yard too long.

roster.name: a lattice-hound
roster.look: A long shape of joined light running on the lattice lines under the ground, surfacing where it wants to, the size of a horse and very fast. It follows the lines from the gate toward wherever the holder keeps their people, and the lines lead everywhere.
roster.danger: It hunts the holder, not the yard. It comes up under their hold, their camp, their barracks at the gate, and it takes the ones who gave the order to hold it. It goes back down the line when it has taken enough, and it knows who it came for.
pressures: WARD (cut it off from the lattice)
MOVE (don't be where the lines go)
SHAPE (a line that leads it home)

Every people tells some version of this; the Crossing's porters say it to every new lord who looks at the Hub Yard too long.

roster.name: the Keeper of the Arch
roster.look: The gate itself stands up. The arch unfolds from its footings into something tall and many-jointed, the lattice lines running up it like veins, and it looks at the holder's banner over the yard with a patience older than any people.
roster.danger: It takes the gate back. Everything the holder built within sight of it comes down; everyone the holder left to guard it is thrown back through the arch to somewhere else on the network. Then it folds itself down into an arch again, and the gate is nobody's.
pressures: SHAPE (give the gate back, formally, before it finishes)

It is not a person and the bestiary's first law says so. It needs a move set, and the CLASS is where that lives — six classes, six distinct fictions, six kits. ⚠️ AND TWO CLASSES ALREADY CARRY ENGINE MEANING: `deathSave.notForClasses` bars `feral_construct` and `made_weapon`, so the classes were already load-bearing and nothing else read them. ⛔ THREE MOVES EACH, same as the contribution-family archetypes — a two-move opponent is a coin flip.
